correctness.rationale: The suffix constraints for a linked type-C Gale interval are equivalent bijectively to binary states y_i= sum_{j>=i}x_j-|S cap [i,n]| in {0,1}, with y_{n+1}=0, and x_i=s_i+y_i-y_{i+1}. For ordered vertex pairs the four possible paired y states and allowed 0/1 monotone transitions yield the stated M_0(z), M_1(z), with discrepancy exponent |(a-b)-(c-d)| in {0,1}; therefore 1^T product M e_00 enumerates ALL ordered vertex-pair squared Euclidean distances for every n>=3. Independent Python exhaustive binary feasible-set enumeration matches independently computed four-state polynomials coefficient-for-coefficient for all 510 profiles from n2..9. Squared distance n requires complementary vertices; applying each odd/even suffix to both endpoints gives necessary and sufficient two-position block criteria, 2^floor(n/2) eligible profiles and 2^(ceil(n/2)-1) unordered antipodal pairs each. Strict convexity excludes interior diameter endpoints. Finite enumeration corroborates but is not the unbounded proof.
residual_risks: The matrices count standard-coordinate vertex pairs, not arbitrary-point distances or any affinely rescaled realization.
